Read our Privacy notice A pair of honeytrap killers who drugged men seeking escort services to steal from them have been jailed for 17 years after two victims died. Adina Mihai , 31, posed as a sex worker and arranged to meet men at their homes in an organised operation with her partner Madalin Dumitru, 30. Between August 2024 and July 2025, Mihai would ply the men with alcohol spiked with date-rape drug gamma-butyrolactone (GBL) before searching their home for cash, jewellery and watches to steal while Dumitru waited in a car nearby, a court heard. However Malcolm King, 80, died after the encounter in Bagendon, Gloucestershire, in August 2024. At first, Gloucestershire Police treated his death as non-suspicious because he had a pre-existing heart condition. But the case was re-opened after Thames Valley Police discovered father of one Gary Mouat, 37, had been poisoned with the drug when he died in similar circumstances in Banbury, Oxfordshire, almost a year later. The Romanian couple had been due to stand trial at Oxford Crown Court this summer but admitted to two counts of manslaughter on the second day of the hearing. They also pleaded guilty to poisoning two other men with GBL in July 2025, who survived. Police believe other victims may have been targeted by the pair and have urged them to come forward. Jailing them on Thursday, judge Mrs Justice Brunner KC said the couple had formed a joint plan to “covertly drug the men” but accepted that they did not know that anyone had died as they continued their scam. open image in gallery Malcolm King, 80, was killed at his home in Gloucestershire ( Thames Valley Police ) “However, if you had stopped for a moment to consider the risks, as you should have done, you would have realised that you were creating a high risk of serious injury or death every time you administered that drug,” she said. “If you had done the most cursory research you would know that GBL can be extremely toxic.” She added: “You left each victim alone in a state of deep unconsciousness and a moment’s thought could and should have led to the realisation that they might never come round.” Mihai, wearing a polkadot dress, wiped away tears as the judge addressed her. Dumitru, wearing a pale blue tracksuit, was also emotional in the dock as the sentence was handed down. Prosecutor Julian Evans KC told the court Mihai advertised escort and massage services on the Vivastreet website. Once victims made contact, Dumitru would drive Mihai to their home and give them alcohol laced with GBL, which rapidly converts to a powerful sedative once in the body. After scouring the property for items to steal, the pair would leave the men unconscious and alone in their homes. “Put simply, the defendants were willing to act in this way out of greed,” Mr Evans told the court. “Together, they no doubt drew comfort from the shared belief that they could proceed with their obviously criminal activity safe in the knowledge that their victims were highly unlikely to report what had happened to them to the police. “That confidence drew upon the obviously sensitive and embarrassing nature of the activity each victim believed they had agreed to. Namely, meeting a stranger at their home for the purposes of engaging in sexual activity in exchange for money.” The killers both sobbed in the dock as their victim’s family members read out moving personal statements. In a pre-recorded message played to court Mr Mouat’s son, aged nine, asked them: “Why did you have to kill my daddy, you could have just taken the money, he was really kind, he would have given it to you. He was my daddy and now he's gone.” open image in gallery Gary Mouat, 37, was drugged at his home in Oxfordfordshire ( Thames Valley Police ) His mother, Mr Mouat’s wife Louise, paid tribute to her late husband as a “friendly, funny and kind man” with a “huge personality”. “You’ve destroyed my present and taken away my future,” she told the killers. “You’ve taken away the plan for Gary and me to grow our family.” The court heard Mr Mouat had made contact with Mihai through her Vivastreet account on 12 July 2025, while his wife and son were away for the weekend. In messages sent while waiting in a car outside Mr Mouat’s home that night, Dumitru told Mihai to put the victim “to sleep”, Mr Evans said. He later told her see if he had a watch or any jewellery, as well as cash. Mr Mouat was found dead the following day by two friends who went to check on him. The court heard that Mr King, a wealthy man who wore a valuable 18ct gold Rolex Oyster watch, had made contact with Mihai’s Vivastreet account on the morning of 20 August 2024. CCTV footage shows the parking near his house that evening, before Mihai entered the property. open image in gallery Malcom King's 18ct gold Rolex Oyster watch was stolen by his killers ( Thames Valley Police ) Data from the 80-year-old’s pacemaker show he died around an hour after the couple left the area, having stolen his watch. He was found dead by his housekeeper the following morning and Mihai’s DNA was found on one of two wine glasses left at the scene. In a tearful statement, his daughter Caroline King told the court that she had not always had an easy relationship with her father. “The defendants did not simply unlawfully take my father's life,” she said. “They stole the future that both he and I still had the possibility of writing together. “They took away every conversation we will now never have, every opportunity to understand one another and every chance to make peace with our past. “I do not know whether reconciliation would ever have happened. The hardest part is that I will never be allowed to find out.” open image in gallery Mihai's DNA was found on a wine glass at Malcolm King's home ( Thames Valley Police ) Mr King’s sister, Jacky Seagroatt, said she is haunted by the way in which he died. “Nothing that happens in this courtroom can bring my brother back,” she said. “Nothing can replace the love, generosity and loyalty he so freely gave to me, to our family and to so many others. “I ask only that the devastating consequences of these offences are fully recognised. Malcolm’s life mattered. He was loved. His death has left a wound in our family that will never heal. I will carry the pain of losing my brother for the rest of my life.” Mihai took another Rolex, worth up to £14,500, from another victim who survived the drugging, the court heard. She stole some jewellery, aftershave and documents from a fourth surviving victim. In mitigation, Mihai’s lawyer told the court she “did not realise that GBL could cause the harm that it did” until she was told of the two men’s deaths. “She asked me to relay to the court her shock, shame and sorrow for the terrible harm that has been caused,” Elouise Marshall KC said. open image in gallery The couple were jailed at Oxford Crown Court ( AFP/Getty ) Gurdeep Garcha KC, for Dumitru, said the defendant had shown “genuine remorse” and taken responsibility for his actions, adding that the impact on Mr Mouat’s son had “particular resonance” because he is a father to three children aged 13, 11 and six. “He has asked me to publically express his deep regret at what he has done and he would wish, through me, to unconditionally apologise to all of the families of the victims and everybody affected,” he said. Thames Valley Police senior investigating officer, Detective Inspector Michael Roddy, said the pair deliberately exploited men for financial gain, showing “a complete disregard for the devastating consequences of their actions”. “Their offending was calculated, predatory and ultimately cost two innocent men their lives,” he added. "Gary Mouat and Malcolm King were much-loved family members whose deaths have left lasting pain for those who knew them.” Gloucestershire Constabulary’s senior investigating officer, Detective Inspector Adam Stacey, said the pair callously gambled with the lives of their victims. He encouraged any other victims who believe they may have been targeted by the pair to come forward. "I would urge these men to contact police and would like to reassure them that their report will be dealt with sensitively and discreetly,” he said. Photograph: AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen The Bryson fire burns in Malibu, California, on Thursday. Photograph: AFP/Getty Images California California brushfires force evacuations and tens of thousands of power shutoffs Hot, windy weather stokes fires in southern California as utilities shut off power to 150,000 customers as precaution Guardian staff and agencies Fri 16 Oct 2026 09.31 EDT Last modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 10.45 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Several brushfires stoked by hot, windy weather forced evacuations in southern California , and tens of thousands of people woke up in the dark after their electricity was turned off. A rapidly spreading blaze in Malibu, west of Los Angeles, prompted evacuation orders and warnings for a large swathe of the Santa Monica Mountains. Firefighters also worked to contain fires in the city of Azusa, north of LA, and Camp Pendleton, the large military base north of San Diego. In the Santa Monica mountains, more than 285 firefighters battled the Bryson fire overnight, which grew to about 200 acres (81 hectares) and threatened a Los Angeles county juvenile detention and rehabilitative facility. Fire officials planned to give an update on Friday morning. A large cloud of black smoke over the hilltops could be seen on nearby cameras and miles away. Wind gusts of up to 30mph (48km/h) were reported early Friday and were forecast to increase, the National Weather Service said. With humidity levels dropping, “this will favor a critical fire weather threat,” the service said. The wind-driven fire in Azusa burned more than 40 acres (16 hectares) on Thursday and briefly prompted evacuation orders for a neighborhood in the foothills of the San Gabriel mountains. Forward progress on that blaze has been stopped. At Camp Pendleton, evacuation orders were issued in the Las Flores area of the military base on Thursday afternoon, but lifted by evening, military officials said in a statement. California is facing several days of extreme fire-risk weather, with dry conditions, high temperatures and gusty winds intensifying the risk that a fire quickly gets under control. Dry, warm and gusty north-east winds known as Santa Anas, which blow from the interior of southern California toward the coast and offshore, were forecast in the south of the state, with the strongest winds expected through Friday afternoon. “It’s a pretty widespread event of elevated fire weather, so the whole SoCal region should really be on alert,” said Rose Schoenfeld, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service. Because some of the state’s worst wildfires in recent years have been sparked by power equipment, utilities proactively shut off power to more than 150,000 customers across the state. In Los Angeles, the city’s mayor, Karen Bass, who faced criticism for her city’s response to deadly fires in 2025, directed the fire department to deploy personnel and equipment ahead of the winds. The fire department also requested assistance from the state’s office of emergency services. In January 2025, fires in the Palisades and Altadena neighborhoods, which were fanned by Santa Ana winds, killed more than 30 people and destroyed thousands of homes. Schoenfeld said the Santa Ana winds are not going to be as strong as during those fires, when they were gusting 60mph to 100mph. Photograph: Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images Republicans Vivek Ramaswamy discontinues attack ad that prompted wave of revulsion Candidate for Ohio governor confirms campaign no longer airing ad that smeared rival and was defended by Trump Robert Mackey Thu 29 Oct 2026 21.10 EDT Last modified on Thu 29 Oct 2026 21.12 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Vivek Ramaswamy, the Republican nominee for Ohio governor, confirmed on Thursday that his campaign is no longer airing an attack ad that features the estranged mother of his Democratic opponent, Amy Acton. The ad prompted a wave of revulsion since Acton’s mother, Donna Arthur, lost custody of her daughter in 1978, when her second husband, Cledith Arthur, was charged with raping her daughter between the ages of 10 and 12. Asked by a reporter in Vandalia, Ohio if his campaign had stopped running the ad, Ramaswamy said : “It ran to completion and we put up four other ads.” DoJ reportedly issues subpoenas over same-name Alaska candidates Read more “But what I will say is that for all of the discussion around 30-second ads, I would love, even for this final close, for this campaign to really be about policy,” Ramaswamy added, before criticizing his opponent for not debating him. Ramaswamy’s campaign had announced last week that it would spend $4m to broadcast the ad , despite criticism from Democrats and Republicans after court records showed that Acton’s mother, who called her daughter “a liar”, had fled the state with her husband when her daughter accused him of rape. In an interview with the anti-abortion group Operation Rescue in 2020, when Acton was leading Ohio’s response to the Covid pandemic, Acton’s mother said that she was aware that, before she married him, Cledith Arthur had previously been accused of raping his own daughter. Ramaswamy’s reference to “30-second ads” referred to the length of the ad after his campaign edited the original 60-second version, to remove the allegation from Acton’s mother that her daughter had lied about the family having lived in a tent with Arthur when she was a child. Court records from the time indicated that Cledith Arthur had, indeed, lived in a tent at the time of his arrest on rape charges. Donald Trump repeatedly defended the ad, including at a rally with Ramaswamy on Wednesday, while refusing to acknowledge that the serious child rape allegation was relevant to the credibility of Acton’s mother. Reporting from NBC News and Zeteo suggests that Acton’s mother has suffered from mental health challenges and was found living in her car with dozens of cats , which troubled some people involved in producing the ad for Ramaswamy’s campaign. “How far will Vivek Ramaswamy go?” Acton’s campaign asked in a new ad on the controversy released earlier on Thursday. “To become governor, he’ll smear his opponent for being raped by her stepfather when she was just 10 years old – exploiting the sexual abuse of a child and spending millions lying to you about it,” the ad warns Ohio voters. Acton also addressed Ramaswamy’s attack ad at an event on Thursday. “You’ve probably all heard by now, if you didn’t know, a little bit about my childhood,” she told supporters. “My brother and I experienced a lot of things, a lot of abuse and a lot of neglect. We were frequent flyers in children’s services, ended up living in a tent in the middle of winter.” “My opponent has now chosen to exploit my childhood intentionally,” she continued. “He’s doing it in a desperate attempt to save his struggling campaign. But I’ll tell you, Mr Ramaswamy, it’s not going to work.” Explore more on these topics Republicans Ohio US midterm elections 2026 US politics news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness
